bio-cell-01-c2.text: National Human Genome Research Institute. Chromosome (Genetics Glossary). genome.gov (NHGRI).
bio-cell-01-c2.quote: Humans have 22 pairs of numbered chromosomes (autosomes) and one pair of sex chromosomes (XX or XY), for a total of 46.
bio-cell-01-c2.claim: You have 46 of them (23 pairs) in every body cell.

bio-cell-02-c3.text: Meiosis. Talking Glossary of Genomic and Genetic Terms, National Human Genome Research Institute.
bio-cell-02-c3.quote: During meiosis, each diploid cell undergoes two rounds of division to yield four haploid daughter cells
bio-cell-02-c3.claim: Unlike mitosis, it has two divisions and produces four daughter cells, each with half the chromosomes (23 in humans, not 46).

bio-cell-04-c1.text: Susanna Törnroth-Horsefield, Richard Neutze (2008). Opening and closing the metabolite gate. Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.
bio-cell-04-c1.quote: On any given day you turn over your body weight equivalent in ATP, the principal energy currency of the cell.
bio-cell-04-c1.claim: Your body recycles your body-weight equivalent of ATP every day.

bio-cell-04-c3.text: Andrew H. Knoll, Martin A. Nowak (2017). The timetable of evolution. Science Advances.
bio-cell-04-c3.quote: Oxygen concentrations in the atmosphere and surface oceans first rose in the Great Oxygenation Event (GOE) 2.4 billion years ago
bio-cell-04-c3.claim: Before the Great Oxygenation Event ~2.4 billion years ago, Earth's air was almost oxygen-free.

bio-cell-06-c2.text: Claire T. Friel, Jonathon Howard (2012). Coupling of kinesin ATP turnover to translocation and microtubule regulation: one engine, many machines. Journal of Muscle Research and Cell Motility.
bio-cell-06-c2.quote: Kinesin takes one 8-nm step for each ATP that it hydrolyzes.
bio-cell-06-c2.claim: Each step (about 8 nm for kinesin) is powered by ATP hydrolysis.

bio-cell-06-c3.text: Peter Friedl, Katarina Wolf (2010). Plasticity of cell migration: a multiscale tuning model. Journal of Cell Biology.
bio-cell-06-c3.quote: In both cases, subsequent to leading edge protrusion, actomyosin contraction leads to retraction of the cell rear and translocation of the cell body
bio-cell-06-c3.claim: Crawling cells extend an actin-based protrusion (lamellipodium) at the leading edge, form new adhesions with the substrate, contract the cell body forward via myosin, and release rear adhesions.

bio-cell-07-c1.text: Nobel Assembly at Karolinska Institutet (2001). Press release: The Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine 2001. NobelPrize.org.
bio-cell-07-c1.quote: Instead they can exit from the cell cycle and enter a resting stage (G0).
bio-cell-07-c1.claim: Cells can exit the cycle into G0: quiescent state.

bio-cell-07-c2.text: The Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine 2001. NobelPrize.org.
bio-cell-07-c2.quote: The Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine 2001 was awarded jointly to Leland H. Hartwell, Tim Hunt and Sir Paul M. Nurse "for their discoveries of key regulators of the cell cycle"
bio-cell-07-c2.claim: Hartwell, Nurse, and Hunt shared the 2001 Medicine Nobel for the cyclin/CDK story.

bio-cell-07-c3.text: Hany E. Marei, Asmaa Althani, Nahla Afifi, et al (2021). p53 signaling in cancer progression and therapy. Cancer Cell International.
bio-cell-07-c3.quote: The TP53 gene is mutated in approximately half of all human malignancies, including those of the breast, colon, lung, liver, prostate, bladder, and skin.
bio-cell-07-c3.claim: p53 is mutated in about half of all cancers.

bio-cell-08-c1.text: Susan Elmore (2007). Apoptosis: A Review of Programmed Cell Death. Toxicologic Pathology.
bio-cell-08-c1.quote: Because apoptotic cells do not release their cellular constituents into the surrounding interstitial tissue and are quickly phagocytosed by macrophages or adjacent normal cells, there is essentially no inflammatory reaction
bio-cell-08-c1.claim: Cells condense, fragment into membrane-bound apoptotic bodies, and are engulfed by phagocytes without inflammation.

bio-cell-08-c2.text: Susan Elmore (2007). Apoptosis: A Review of Programmed Cell Death. Toxicologic Pathology.
bio-cell-08-c2.quote: Necrosis is an uncontrolled and passive process that usually affects large fields of cells whereas apoptosis is controlled and energy-dependent and can affect individual or clusters of cells.
bio-cell-08-c2.claim: Necrosis is unregulated cell death from severe injury: cells swell, burst, release contents, trigger inflammation.

bio-cell-08-c3.text: Lei Zhang, Louise E. Pitcher, Matthew J. Yousefzadeh, et al (2022). Cellular senescence: a key therapeutic target in aging and diseases. Journal of Clinical Investigation.
bio-cell-08-c3.quote: Many SnCs secrete a wide spectrum of bioactive factors, including inflammatory cytokines, chemokines, growth factors, matrix metalloproteinases, lipids, nucleotides, extracellular vesicles, and soluble factors, termed the senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP)
bio-cell-08-c3.claim: Senescent cells are metabolically active and secrete inflammatory factors (the senescence-associated secretory phenotype, SASP).

bio-cell-02-c1.text: Nobel Assembly at Karolinska Institutet (2001). Press release: The Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine 2001. NobelPrize.org.
bio-cell-02-c1.quote: In the first phase (G1) the cell grows and becomes larger. When it has reached a certain size it enters the next phase (S), in which DNA-synthesis takes place.
bio-cell-02-c1.claim: It's split into G1 (growth), S (DNA synthesis), and G2 (preparation).

bio-cell-02-c2.text: Mitosis. Talking Glossary of Genomic and Genetic Terms, National Human Genome Research Institute.
bio-cell-02-c2.quote: Mitosis is generally followed by equal division of the cell’s content into two daughter cells that have identical genomes.
bio-cell-02-c2.claim: Mitosis produces two genetically identical daughter cells.

bio-cell-03-c2.text: Ruben G. Contreras, Antonio Torres-Carrillo, Catalina Flores-Maldonado, et al (2024). Na+/K+-ATPase: More than an Electrogenic Pump. International Journal of Molecular Sciences.
bio-cell-03-c2.quote: Its primary role is to transport sodium (Na+) and potassium (K+) ions across the cell membrane, using energy from ATP hydrolysis.
bio-cell-03-c2.claim: The most famous example is the sodium-potassium pump, which keeps cells low in sodium and high in potassium.

bio-cell-03-c3.text: Membrane transport into and out of the cell. Nature Education (Scitable).
bio-cell-03-c3.quote: Here, a transport vesicle from the Golgi or elsewhere in the cell merges its membrane with the plasma membrane and releases its contents.
bio-cell-03-c3.claim: Exocytosis: vesicles inside the cell merge with the membrane and dump their contents outside.

bio-cell-05-c2.text: Nobel Assembly at Karolinska Institutet (1994). Press release: The Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine 1994. NobelPrize.org.
bio-cell-05-c2.quote: The amplifier generates large amounts of the intracellular “second messenger”, for example cyclic AMP.
bio-cell-05-c2.claim: Typically a cascade: receptor activates an enzyme, which activates more enzymes, which activate more, amplifying the original signal massively.

bio-cell-05-c3.text: Nobel Assembly at Karolinska Institutet (1989). Press release: The Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine 1989. NobelPrize.org.
bio-cell-05-c3.quote: Disturbances in one or some of these so-called oncogenes (Gk ónco(s) bulk, mass) can lead to transformation of a normal cell into a tumor cell and result in cancer.
bio-cell-05-c3.claim: Mutations in oncogenes (growth-promoting) or tumor suppressor genes (growth-restricting) can lock the 'divide' signal ON or break the 'don't divide' signal.
